questions.q: Design a URL shortener like Bitly.
questions.a: Clarify traffic, custom aliases, expiration, analytics, and redirect latency. A strong design includes an API layer, ID generator, mapping store, cache for hot URLs, and async analytics pipeline. Discuss collision avoidance, key size, read-heavy optimization, and database sharding.

questions.q: Design a distributed rate limiter for backend APIs.
questions.a: Compare fixed window, sliding window, leaky bucket, and token bucket. Use Redis or a similar fast store for distributed counters, expiration, and atomic updates. Mention per-user and per-IP limits, fairness, bursts, failure fallback, and observability.

questions.q: Design a notification service for email, SMS, and push.
questions.a: Separate ingestion, template rendering, queueing, provider dispatch, retries, and status tracking. Good answers include provider adapters, dead-letter queues, idempotency keys, user preference handling, and delivery analytics.

questions.q: Design a file upload service for large files.
questions.a: Use direct-to-object-storage uploads with pre-signed URLs, multipart upload, resumability, metadata persistence, and background scanning. Mention large-file retries, chunk validation, CDN integration, and access control.

questions.q: Design a chat backend for one-to-one and group messaging.
questions.a: Break the system into connection service, message write path, fan-out, persistence, delivery acknowledgments, and unread state. Cover ordering, offline delivery, retries, read receipts, and conversation partitioning.

questions.q: Design a social media news feed backend.
questions.a: Explain post write path, follower graph, feed generation, ranking, caching, and pagination. Discuss fan-out on write versus fan-out on read, celebrity-user issues, and latency versus storage tradeoffs.

questions.q: Design an e-commerce cart and checkout backend.
questions.a: Split responsibilities into cart, pricing, inventory, order, payment, and notification services. A strong answer covers stock reservation, idempotent checkout, saga orchestration, retries, and anti-oversell protection.

questions.q: Design a ride-booking backend like Uber/Ola.
questions.a: Focus on rider service, driver service, location updates, matching engine, trip state machine, pricing, and notifications. Mention geospatial indexing, surge pricing, event streams, and trip consistency.

questions.q: Design a distributed job queue system.
questions.a: Discuss producers, queue broker, workers, visibility timeout, retries, DLQ, scheduling, and autoscaling. Strong answers include idempotent job processing, deduplication, ordering semantics, and monitoring.

questions.q: Design an API gateway for microservices.
questions.a: Include routing, authentication, rate limiting, request aggregation, logging, retries, circuit breakers, and service discovery. Cover how to keep the gateway thin and avoid making it a bottleneck.

questions.q: Design a search autocomplete backend.
questions.a: Use prefix indexing, tries, or a search engine for suggestion retrieval. Mention ranking by popularity, typo tolerance, caching hot prefixes, periodic rebuilding, and tight latency requirements.

questions.q: Design a video streaming backend.
questions.a: Separate upload, transcoding, metadata, storage, authorization, playback manifest generation, and CDN delivery. Mention adaptive bitrate streaming, pre-signed URLs, abuse prevention, and analytics.

questions.q: Design an authentication and session management service.
questions.a: Cover signup, login, token/session issuance, refresh strategy, revocation, password resets, MFA, and device/session tracking. Compare stateless JWT and stateful sessions and mention secure cookie handling.

questions.q: Design a password reset workflow.
questions.a: Generate short-lived, single-use reset tokens stored securely or signed with strict expiry. Include rate limiting, audit logs, email delivery, invalidation of old tokens, and session revocation after password change.

questions.q: Design a backend for live comments on a stream.
questions.a: Use WebSockets or SSE for low-latency delivery, moderate messages asynchronously, and store a durable comment log for replay. Discuss ordering, fan-out, spam protection, and room partitioning.

questions.q: Design a backend for collaborative document editing.
questions.a: Discuss real-time sync, conflict resolution using OT or CRDTs, document snapshots, operation logs, and presence tracking. Mention persistence, autosave, and scaling by document room.

questions.q: Design a metrics collection backend like Prometheus-lite.
questions.a: Explain data ingestion, label/index storage, time-series compression, retention, downsampling, and query APIs. Mention cardinality explosion, batching, and pull versus push tradeoffs.

questions.q: Design a centralized logging backend.
questions.a: Break the system into log shippers, ingestion pipeline, parsing/enrichment, indexing, storage tiers, and query UI. Cover retention, backpressure, partitioning, and cost control.

questions.q: Design a metrics alerting system.
questions.a: Include alert rule storage, periodic evaluation, deduplication, suppression, escalation, and notification delivery. Strong answers discuss noisy alerts, grouping, and high availability of the evaluator.

questions.q: Design a distributed cache service.
questions.a: Talk about key partitioning, replication, eviction policies, TTLs, cache invalidation, and consistency with backing stores. Mention hot keys, rebalancing, and cache stampede protection.

questions.q: Design a leader election service.
questions.a: Use consensus-based coordination or lease-based leadership through a reliable store. Explain heartbeats, fencing tokens, split-brain prevention, and failover time.

questions.q: Design a service discovery system.
questions.a: Discuss service registration, health checks, client-side versus server-side discovery, DNS-based discovery, and stale endpoint handling. Mention consistency and failure detection tradeoffs.

questions.q: Design a feature flag service.
questions.a: Core parts are flag definition, targeting rules, rollout percentages, evaluation SDKs, caching, and audit history. Mention low-latency reads, eventual consistency, and kill switches.

questions.q: Design a distributed configuration management service.
questions.a: Cover config versioning, safe rollout, watches/push updates, rollback, access control, and audit logs. Discuss caching and what happens if clients cannot reach the config service.

questions.q: Design a payment processing backend.
questions.a: Split into order creation, payment intent, gateway integration, retries, webhook handling, ledger entries, and reconciliation. Mention idempotency, fraud checks, PCI scope reduction, and partial failures.

questions.q: Design a ledger service for financial transactions.
questions.a: Use immutable double-entry records, account balances derived from postings, idempotent transaction APIs, and strong auditability. Cover consistency, replay, reconciliation, and backfills.

questions.q: Design an invoice generation backend.
questions.a: Include billing rules, invoice generation jobs, PDF rendering, tax calculation integration, storage, and notification. Mention versioned invoices, corrections, and scheduled billing cycles.

questions.q: Design a subscription billing system.
questions.a: Discuss plans, recurring cycles, trial periods, upgrades, downgrades, proration, payment retries, and dunning workflows. Strong answers include entitlements and invoice history.

questions.q: Design a webhook delivery platform.
questions.a: Store outbound events durably, sign payloads, retry on failure with exponential backoff, and expose delivery history. Mention deduplication, replay tooling, and protecting receivers from bursts.

questions.q: Design an event bus for microservices.
questions.a: Talk about topic partitioning, consumer groups, ordering guarantees, schema evolution, replay, and retention. Compare at-least-once versus exactly-once semantics and discuss idempotent consumers.

questions.q: Design a pub/sub messaging backend.
questions.a: Include publishers, topics, subscriptions, durable message storage, pull or push delivery, ack handling, retries, and filtering. Mention fan-out scale and backpressure.

questions.q: Design a cron scheduling service.
questions.a: Support time-based job definitions, persistent schedules, distributed execution, leader election, retries, and exactly-once or at-least-once guarantees. Mention clock skew and missed execution recovery.

questions.q: Design an email delivery backend.
questions.a: Separate template management, send APIs, queueing, provider integrations, retries, bounce tracking, and suppression lists. Discuss rate limiting, warm-up, and analytics.

questions.q: Design an SMS delivery backend.
questions.a: Cover provider abstraction, retries, delivery receipts, opt-out handling, throttling, regional routing, and fraud prevention. Mention compliance and cost-aware fallback provider selection.

questions.q: Design a push notification backend for mobile apps.
questions.a: Include device token registration, provider integration, targeting, retries, collapse keys, preference filters, and analytics. Mention invalid token cleanup and batching.

questions.q: Design a backend for user activity tracking and analytics.
questions.a: Use an event ingestion API, durable queue, stream processors, warehouse or analytics store, and aggregation jobs. Cover schema evolution, sampling, deduplication, and privacy concerns.

questions.q: Design a recommendation backend.
questions.a: Discuss event collection, feature generation, candidate generation, ranking, caching, and feedback loops. Mention online versus offline computation and freshness tradeoffs.

questions.q: Design a backend for product search.
questions.a: Include indexing, faceted filters, typo tolerance, ranking, inventory and price freshness, and query caching. Mention denormalized search documents and incremental reindexing.

questions.q: Design a backend for order tracking.
questions.a: Model order states, shipment events, notifications, and a timeline API. Discuss event sourcing versus current-state storage, idempotent updates, and integration with external logistics systems.

questions.q: Design a backend for inventory management.
questions.a: Handle stock updates, reservations, reconciliation, warehousing, and oversell prevention. Strong answers cover strong consistency for critical operations, event streams, and audit trails.

questions.q: Design a backend for coupon and promotion management.
questions.a: Include rule definitions, eligibility checks, redemption limits, concurrency protection, expiration, and abuse prevention. Mention caching and auditability for business disputes.

questions.q: Design a backend for user profile storage and retrieval.
questions.a: Discuss profile write/read APIs, schema evolution, privacy fields, indexing, caching, and searchability. Mention separating frequently changing counters from core profile data.

questions.q: Design a backend for session-based real-time presence.
questions.a: Track online users with heartbeats, expiring keys, and fan-out updates for interested clients. Cover disconnect detection, multi-device state, and eventual consistency.

questions.q: Design a backend for document storage and sharing like Google Drive-lite.
questions.a: Split the problem into metadata service, object storage, permission model, sharing links, versioning, and sync notifications. Mention large files, preview generation, and ACL enforcement.

questions.q: Design a backend for image processing and thumbnail generation.
questions.a: Accept uploads, enqueue processing jobs, generate variants, store metadata, and serve through CDN. Good answers mention deduplication, retries, and async processing for user responsiveness.

questions.q: Design a backend for audit logging.
questions.a: Store immutable append-only events with actor, action, entity, timestamp, and metadata. Discuss searchability, retention, tamper resistance, and access control for sensitive audit data.

questions.q: Design a backend for API key management.
questions.a: Support key creation, hashing at rest, scope restrictions, rotation, revocation, usage limits, and analytics. Mention secure display-once flows and service-to-service authentication patterns.

questions.q: Design a backend for multi-tenant SaaS data isolation.
questions.a: Compare shared-table, shared-schema, and isolated-database approaches. Cover tenant-aware auth, noisy-neighbor protection, migration strategy, and per-tenant configuration.

questions.q: Design a backend for content moderation workflow.
questions.a: Use ingestion, moderation queue, automated classifiers, human review tooling, action history, and appeal flows. Mention false positives, SLA tiers, and policy versioning.

questions.q: Design a backend for a support ticketing system.
questions.a: Model ticket creation, assignment, comments, SLA tracking, notifications, search, and escalations. Strong answers cover concurrency on updates, audit trails, and integrations with email/chat.

questions.q: Design a backend for a URL crawl and indexing system.
questions.a: Break into scheduler, frontier queue, crawler workers, politeness rules, deduplication, content parsing, and indexing. Mention robots.txt, rate limiting per domain, and incremental recrawl.

questions.q: Design a backend for a map/reverse-geocoding service.
questions.a: Discuss geospatial indexing, tile or region partitioning, query APIs, caching, and offline data updates. Mention precision, latency, and handling hot urban regions.

questions.q: Design a backend for leaderboard ranking.
questions.a: Use sorted sets or ranking indexes for top-N retrieval, score updates, and pagination around a player. Mention seasonal resets, tie-breaking, and anti-cheat validations.

questions.q: Design a backend for OTP generation and verification.
questions.a: Generate short-lived codes, throttle requests, hash or protect OTP storage, and support multiple delivery channels. Mention replay prevention, expiration, abuse detection, and auditing.

questions.q: Design a backend for a document approval workflow.
questions.a: Include state transitions, reviewers, parallel or sequential approvals, audit history, reminders, and role-based permissions. Mention rejections, versioning, and notifications.
